title: Iran says it captured US drone south of Qeshm Island in Strait of Hormuz
html:
Iran says it captured US drone south of Qeshm Island in Strait of Hormuz

IRGC Navy claims electronic warfare operation forced MQM-170 drone to land intact

Şahin Demir

16 November 2026•Update: 16 November 2026

İSTANBUL

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said Monday that it seized control of a US military drone south of Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz and brought it down intact.

In a statement, its public relations office identified the aircraft as an MQM-170, saying it was intercepted during an electronic warfare operation Monday morning.

The drone was attempting to locate and identify Iranian air defense and electronic warfare systems, the statement alleged.

Iranian forces took control of its guidance system and forced it to land without damage, it added.

The IRGC Navy said it was the fourth drone of this type captured by its electronic warfare and drone command, and the eighth drone brought down intact by IRGC air defenses in the Strait of Hormuz area.

It also claimed its forces had intercepted, destroyed or disabled other US drones, including MQ-9s, MQ-1s and Lucas attack drones.

There was no US comment on the Iranian claim.

Iran has made similar announcements in recent weeks. In early November, the IRGC reported using electronic warfare systems against MQM-170 drones near Qeshm Island. The US military rejected an earlier Iranian account of a drone capture.

​​​​​​​Qeshm, Iran’s largest island, lies along the northern approaches to the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for oil and gas shipments from Gulf countries to international markets.
summary: IRGC Navy claims electronic warfare operation forced MQM-170 drone to land intact | Anadolu
